text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- CNPF employers federation criticises the government's economic plans, says investment is main weakness in French economy.
-- Prime Minister's office confirms re-election of Eramet mining group chairman and names an assessment committee to evaluate nickel resources in New Caledonia.
-- A pickup in Airbus [ARBU.CN] sales expected to create up to 4,000 jobs in France.
-- Aircraft engine manufacturer Snecma [SNEC.CN] needs a two-billion-franc recapitalisation, according to chairman Jean-Paul Bechat.
-- An extroardinary meeting of Eurotunnel shareholders today is expected to approve the company's financial restructuring prospectus -- provided a quorum is present for the meeting to take place.
-- An audit of public finances, to be unveiled on July 21, is expected by some sources to reveal a French public deficit of 3.6 percent to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product.
-- Head of National Assembly Finance Committee Henri Emmanuelli launches an information study on European automobile sector, and the implementation of a 1991 agreement between Europe and Japan.
-- Insurance broker Gras Savoye near alliance with British partner, group Sedgwick is seen as the most likely candidate.
-- CGIP increases stake in Cap Gemini computer services group to 30 percent from 20 percent.
-- 1998 deficit forecast above four percent of GDP according to a confidential note from former Prime Minister Alain Juppe to his successor Lionel Jospin on June 2.

-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn to tap previous government's frozen spending lines to finance some 11.1 billion francs new spending, notably a higher "back to school" allowance, improved housing and employment measures.
-- Remy Cointreau stocks skid twelve percent yesterday after it announced its profit fell 70 percent to 36 million francs for the year to end March 1997.
